data.name: Kifayah
data.gender_notes: Kifayah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Fulfillment of needs or requirements. The name Kifayah carries the meaning “Sufficient” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Kifayah usually hope their child will grow to embody sufficient and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A term used in Hadiths to describe a believer who contributes to the needs of the community, and is rewarded with paradise.
data.etymology: Kifayah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sufficient.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kifayah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: كفاية
in_arabic.long_meaning: كفاية هي كلمة عربية مشتقة من الفعل كفى، وتعني الغنية عن غيرها، والاستغناء عن سائر الأمور، وتستخدم في الإسلام لوصف الله سبحانه وتعالى، كما ذکر في القرآن الكريم، وتعبر عن القدرة والكفاية في الحصول على ما يحتاجه الإنسان

in_urdu.name: کفایہ
in_urdu.meaning: کفایہ کا مطلب ہے خود کفیل ہونا
in_urdu.long_meaning: کفایہ ایک عربی لفظ ہے جو کفى سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے خود کفیل ہونا، اور دوسروں کی مدد کی ضرورت نہیں ہے، یہ اسلام میں الله کی وصف کے لیے بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے، جیسا کہ قرآن پاک میں ذکر کیا گیا ہے

in_hindi.name: किफ़ाया
in_hindi.meaning: किफ़ाया का अर्थ है स्वयं पर्याप्त होना
in_hindi.long_meaning: किफ़ाया एक अरबी शब्द है जो कफी से उत्पन्न हुआ है, जिसका अर्थ है स्वयं पर्याप्त होना, और दूसरों की सहायता की आवश्यकता नहीं है, यह इस्लाम में अल्लाह की विशेषता के लिए भी प्रयोग किया जाता है, जैसा कि कुरआन में उल्लेख किया गया है

in_pashto.name: کفایت
in_pashto.long_meaning: کفایت د عربي کلمې څخه اخیستل شوی دی چې د کفی څخه مشتق شوی دی، د کفایت مانا دا دی چې ځانته کفایت کول، او د نورو مرستې ته اړتیا نشته، دا کلمه په اسلام کې د الله تعالی د توصیف لپاره هم کارول کیږي، لکه څنګه چې په قرآن کریم کې ذکر شوی دی

in_english.name: Kifayah
in_english.meaning: Kifayah means being sufficient and self-sufficient
in_english.long_meaning: Kifayah is an Arabic term derived from the root k-f-y, meaning to be sufficient, and is used in Islam to describe Allah's attribute of being self-sufficient, as mentioned in the Quran, and signifies the ability to attain what one needs without reliance on others

data.cultural_impact: The name "Kifayah" holds significant cultural importance in Arabic speaking communities, particularly those that follow the Islamic faith. This moniker emphasizes the idea of collective responsibility and mutual support among individuals and communities. It endorses the concept that every person has a role to play in ensuring the total needs of their community are met. This idea is deeply rooted in Islamic teachings that strongly emphasize the importance of working together and taking care of one another.
data.spiritual_significance: In the religious context, the name "Kifayah" is also associated with fulfilling spiritual needs and obligations. In Islamic theology, the term "Fardh" signifies religious obligations that must be carried out to lead a virtuous life, while "Mustahabb" refers to optional acts that serve to strengthen an individual's connection to God. "Kifayah," particularly in this context, refers to the collective obligation to ensure that the minimum requirement for the performance of Fardh and Mustahabb acts is fulfilled for the entire community. This demonstrates the importance of unity and the recognition that each individual's contribution is essential in upholding the spiritual well-being of the community.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Sufficient" symbolizes Fulfillment of needs or requirements. In Islamic spirituality, bearing the name Kifayah serves as a constant reminder of one's spiritual aspirations and connection to Islamic values of sufficient.

trends: Gaining popularity in Western Muslim communities
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Kifayah remains relevant in modern Muslim society, representing a bridge between traditional Islamic values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Islamic names.

name_in_real_life.story: Aisha Kifayah, a teacher in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, shares that their name Kifayah meaning "Sufficient" has been a source of inspiration throughout their life, motivating them to be a positive influence in their community.
